EduPilot · Product guideContents2

Overview

What EduPilot is

One web application that runs the academic, administrative and financial work of an Engineering or Diploma college, for everyone from the principal to the parent.

7roles, each with its own dashboard
66feature areas described in this guide
7end-to-end workflows
3interface languages: English, Hindi, Telugu

Academic

Departments, programmes, batches, curriculum with L-T-P and credits, timetable, attendance with the 75% rule, marks, results with SGPA and CGPA, outcome attainment.

Administrative

Admissions pipeline, student and staff records, leave, certificates, ID cards, hall tickets, library, hostel, transport, helpdesk, notices.

Financial

Fee structures, invoices, instalments, late fines, counter and online collection, receipts, day book, scholarships.

Outcomes

Placement drives with automatic eligibility, alumni records, a report builder, accreditation data sheets and scheduled email reports.

Built for Indian Engineering (B.Tech, M.Tech) and Diploma (Polytechnic) colleges: semesters, lateral entry, internal and end-semester marks, condonation, backlogs and supplementary exams are part of the design.

EduPilot · Product guideOverview3

Overview

Who uses it

Each person sees only the menu items, records and actions their role allows. The coloured tags below are used throughout this guide.

AdminAdministrator / PrincipalEverything: set-up, people, academics, exams, fees, placements, reports and settings.
HODHead of DepartmentOwn department: students, faculty, curriculum, course allocation, timetable, approvals and results.
FacultyFacultyOwn courses: attendance, marks, study material, syllabus coverage, timetable, leave and class swaps.
AccountsAccounts officerFee structures, invoices, collection, refunds, receipts, day book and closing, scholarships and financial reports.
OfficeOffice staffFront desk: enquiries and admissions, student records, certificates, ID cards, helpdesk, library, hostel and transport. No marks, money or settings.
StudentStudentOwn attendance, timetable, results, fees and online payment, placements, leave, certificates, helpdesk and ID card.
ParentParentRead-only view of their child's attendance, results, fees and timetable, with online fee payment.
SystemEduPilot itselfSteps the system carries out automatically, such as calculating grades, checking eligibility and sending notifications.

Getting started · 1.1

Signing in

One address for the whole college. Each person signs in with their college email and sees only what their role allows.

How it works

  1. 1Open the college's EduPilot address
    2. ›
  2. 2Enter college email and password
    3. ›
  3. 3Change the temporary password (first time only)
    4. ›
  4. 4Land on your own dashboard

What it does

  • Seven roles: Administrator / Principal, Head of Department, Faculty, Accounts officer, Office staff, Student and Parent.
  • New students start with their roll number as the password, and new staff with their employee ID. Both must choose a new password at first sign-in.
  • Forgot password sends a single-use link by email, valid for 30 minutes.
  • An account locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords.
  • Staff can turn on two-step sign-in: after the password, a six-digit code is emailed and must be entered.
  • The college name, logo and photo on this page come from Branding & settings.

Who uses it

AdminHODFacultyAccountsOfficeStudentParent

EduPilot · Product guideGetting started6

Getting started · 1.2

The layout of every screen

The same three parts everywhere: the menu on the left, search and your account at the top, and the work area in the middle.

How it works

  1. 1Read My tasks
    2. ›
  2. 2Click a task
    3. ›
  3. 3Finish it on that page
    4. ›
  4. 4The task disappears from the list

What it does

  • Menu: grouped by area (People, Academics, Examinations, Campus, Services, System). It shows only the items your role can use.
  • Greeting banner: today's date, the current term and how far through the term you are, with shortcut buttons for the most common jobs.
  • My tasks: everything waiting on you right now, each one a link to where it gets done. Urgent items are shown in red.
  • Current term card at the bottom of the menu, so nobody works in the wrong semester.
  • A short guided tour runs the first time each person signs in, and can be replayed from My Profile.

Who uses it

AdminHODFacultyAccountsOfficeStudentParent

Search and notifications

Dashboards for each role · 2.1

Principal / Administrator dashboard

The health of the whole institution on one page, with every number linking to the list behind it.

What it does

  • Headline tiles: active students, term attendance, fees collected and faculty strength, each with its trend.
  • Daily attendance chart for the last 30, 60 or 90 days, and an attendance-health gauge showing how many students are eligible, condonable or at risk.
  • Student demographics: gender, admission route and reservation category.
  • Department cards with strength, attendance and pass rate. Click one to open its students.
  • Filter by department, and use Customise to choose which sections appear.
  • Charts expand to full screen and download as images for presentations.
  • The banner and task list appear at once; the figures follow as they are worked out.

Who uses it

Admin

Academic set-up · 4.2

Batches, sections and terms

Group students by admission year and section, and move them forward each semester.

What it does

  • A batch is one admission year and section of a programme, for example BTCSE 2024-A.
  • Promote moves a whole batch to the next semester. After the final semester the batch is graduated and its students become alumni.
  • Academic terms hold the start and end dates. One term is marked current, and it drives attendance, timetable and dashboards.

Who uses it

Admin

How it works

  1. 1Create the term
    2. ›
  2. 2Mark it current
    3. ›
  3. 3Teach and examine
    4. ›
  4. 4Promote each batch
    5. ›
  5. 5Graduate final-year batches
EduPilot · Product guideAcademic set-up31

Academic set-up · 4.3

Promoting a batch

Move a class to the next semester after reviewing who is held back.

How it works

  1. 1Open Promote on the batch
    2. ›
  2. 2Review the ticked students
    3. ›
  3. 3Confirm
    4. ›
  4. 4Detained students move to the junior batch

What it does

  • The review lists every student with CGPA, active backlogs and attendance.
  • Students over the college's backlog limit are already ticked to be held back. The administrator can change any tick before confirming.
  • Held-back students are marked detained and join the batch a year below, so they repeat the year with that class.
  • A final-semester batch graduates instead: its students become alumni, and anyone with a backlog is held back.
  • The backlog limit is set under Administration → Rules. With no limit, everyone is promoted.

Who uses it

Admin

EduPilot · Product guideAcademic set-up32

Daily teaching · 5.1

Taking attendance

Period-wise attendance in a few taps, from a desk or a phone.

What it does

  • The teacher's courses with classes held, last class taken, average attendance and students below 75%.
  • Everyone starts as present; tap a name to mark absent. Late and On-duty are one tap each.
  • Students below 75% are flagged on the sheet. Approved leave and on-duty are pre-filled.
  • Record the topic covered with each class. Past classes can be reopened and corrected, with the change recorded.
  • On a phone, swipe left for absent and right for present. A sheet marked without a connection is kept on the device and uploads when the network returns.

Who uses it

FacultyHOD

How it works

  1. 1Open the course
    2. ›
  2. 2Pick date and period
    3. ›
  3. 3Tap the absentees
    4. ›
  4. 4Save
EduPilot · Product guideDaily teaching37

Daily teaching · 5.2

Shortage report and substitute classes

See who is falling short before the exams, and cover a class when a teacher is away.

What it does

  • The 75% rule with a 65–75% condonation band (both figures can be changed under Administration → Rules): each student is shown as eligible, condonable or detained.
  • Subject-wise percentages for every student in a batch, printable for the notice board.
  • Email alerts to all students below the line, and a Remind parent button that opens WhatsApp with the message already written.
  • Substitutes: the HOD assigns another teacher for a period. It is refused if that teacher already has a class then.

Who uses it

AdminHOD

How it works

    2. ›

  3. 3Students apply for condonation
    4. ›
  4. 4Hall tickets follow the rule

  • The student is notified of the decision in the app and by email.

Section 12

Security, going live and scope

How the data is protected, what the college needs to provide, and what is deliberately outside this product.

Security and reliability

  • Every page and every action checks the person's role on the server, so hidden menu items cannot be reached by typing an address.
  • HODs are limited to their department, teachers to their courses, students and parents to one student's record.
  • Passwords are stored encrypted (hashed). Accounts lock after repeated wrong passwords.
  • Two-step sign-in for staff: an emailed one-time code after the password.
  • A disabled account is locked out immediately, and changing a password signs out other devices.
  • Every change is written to the audit log with the person and the time.
  • The database is backed up automatically every night, the newest 14 are kept, and a second copy can go to another disk. Server errors are logged and emailed to the administrator.

What is needed to go live

A server or cloud machine
EduPilot and its MySQL database run in Docker and restart by themselves after a reboot.
A web address with HTTPS
For example erp.yourcollege.edu.
A mail account (optional)
Any SMTP account, including a free Gmail account with an app password. Without it, emails are stored in the outbox and not delivered.
A Razorpay account (optional)
For real online payments. Without it, fees are collected at the counter and the test checkout is used for demonstrations.
Your data
The College setup checklist imports departments, programmes, batches, curriculum, faculty, fee structures and students from spreadsheets.
Your regulations
Attendance thresholds, pass marks and the grade scale start from common practice and are changed by the administrator on the Rules page.

Not included

  • SMS and automatic WhatsApp messages (paid services). WhatsApp reminders open the staff member's own WhatsApp with the message written.
  • A separate app-store mobile app. The system runs in the phone's browser and can be added to the home screen.
  • Official accreditation templates. The accreditation pages provide the figures to copy into them.

Try it

The demonstration college has 424 students, 32 faculty, 5 departments and 8 programmes, with five semesters of history. Sign in as any role with the demo accounts to follow the workflows in this guide.
